subject: Business
title: Digital Twins in Supply Chains
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Digital Twins in Supply Chains.

hook.text: Unilever built a virtual copy of its entire supply chain. They test disruptions on the copy before they happen in real life.

buildup.text: A digital twin is a real-time virtual model of a physical supply chain, updated with live data.

discovery.text: It lets companies simulate 'what if' scenarios: what if a port closes? What if demand spikes 50%?

twist.text: Building an accurate digital twin requires data from every supplier, carrier, and warehouse.

climax.text: DHL uses digital twins to optimize routes across 220 countries, saving millions in fuel and time.

punchline.text: Test disasters in simulation. Solve them in reality.

quiz.question: What is a supply chain digital twin?
options: A real-time virtual model of a physical supply chain used for simulation
A backup warehouse that mirrors the primary one
A duplicate shipping route for emergencies

details.summary: A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical supply chain that simulates operations in real time using live data feeds. It allows managers to test scenarios, predict disruptions, and optimize decisions without risking real-world consequences.
details.whyItMatters: Digital twins transform supply chain management from reactive to predictive. They let companies simulate the impact of disruptions, demand spikes, or policy changes before they happen, enabling better-informed decisions and faster responses.
takeaways: Digital twins mirror physical supply chains with real-time data integration
Scenario simulation tests responses to disruptions without real-world risk
Predictive analytics identify potential problems before they materialize

faq.question: How does a supply chain digital twin work in practice?
faq.answer: IoT sensors, ERP systems, and logistics platforms feed real-time data into a computational model replicating the physical supply chain. The model simulates material flows, inventory levels, and transit times. Managers run what-if scenarios to evaluate decisions before implementing them.

faq.question: What scenarios can supply chain digital twins simulate?
faq.answer: Supplier failures, port closures, demand surges, new product introductions, warehouse relocations, transportation mode changes, and inventory policy adjustments. Each scenario shows projected impacts on cost, service levels, and lead times across the entire network.
